item.text: {"text":"NextItNet’s residual dilated causal convolutions provide an efficient backbone for expanding historical context, but do not themselves establish which older interactions remain relevant to current intent. The closest recent convolutional result found was TV-Rec: position-dependent, time-variant filters replace fixed kernels and self-attention to capture changing interaction patterns. This supports investigating adaptive convolutional weighting, although it does not establish that a time-decayed NextItNet improves this benchmark. Sources: [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [TV-Rec](https://openreview.net/pdf/e9c3bd1680a3ab54ffe119fc526e57d9835d7b8d.pdf).\n\nPractical hypothesis: retain NextItNet residual causal blocks and jointly learn gates over convolutional features at different dilation depths, allowing each position to emphasize shorter or longer context within one network. Add a nonnegative learned decay conditioned on log elapsed time, using only timestamps observable in each training prefix. A 2026 temporal-prior paper explicitly measures recency relative to the latest observed interaction, avoiding target-timestamp leakage; its decay coefficient is validation-selected, so learned decay remains a proposed extension. Compare adaptive gates and decay through validation ablations rather than assuming stale history is harmful. Preserve padding masks, final nonpadding readout, and one checkpoint per category; keep timestamp handling and architecture identical in training and the predictor writer. Source: [Interaction-Specific Diffusion Scheduling Guided by Temporal Priors](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/15/19/4389)."}
